instructions: Fill a large pot (8 quarts or bigger) with 3 quarts of water. Cut the onion into 6 wedges and smash the 6 garlic cloves with the flat of a knife. Add them to the pot with the 1/3 cup Old Bay and 1 tbsp of thyme leaves. Cover and bring it to a boil over high heat.

Meanwhile, cut the 1 lb potatoes into quarters. Husk the 3 ears of corn and break or cut each one into 3 pieces. Slice the 12 oz sausage into 1 inch pieces. If your shrimp aren't deveined, run a small knife down the back of each one and pull out the dark vein. You can leave the shells on or peel them.
Add the potatoes and the 2 tsp salt to the boiling water. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until a knife goes into a potato with a little resistance left.
Add the corn and cook for 3 minutes. Add the sausage and cook for 4 minutes.
Melt the 4 tbsp butter in a small pan or the microwave. Squeeze 1 1/2 tbsp of juice from half the lemon and stir it into the butter. Cut the other half into wedges. Chop 1 1/2 tbsp of the parsley.
Stir the 1.25 lb shrimp into the pot and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're pink and curled and the flesh has turned from see through to white. Don't walk away. They go rubbery fast.
Scoop out 1/4 cup of the cooking water and set it aside. Drain everything in a colander and fish out the thyme stems.
Spread it all out on a large platter or a rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle the lemon butter over the top and spoon the saved cooking water over it.
Sprinkle on the remaining 1 tsp Old Bay, the 1/4 tsp pepper and the chopped parsley. Taste a potato. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Slice the baguette. Serve with the bread, the lemon wedges and the hot sauce.
method_notes: Both build a big pot of water seasoned with onion, garlic and a half cup of Old Bay, then add potatoes first, corn and sausage next and shrimp last for 2 to 3 minutes, and finish everything on a platter with melted butter. Cooking Classy adds thyme, salts the water, uses andouille and dresses the platter with butter, lemon juice and parsley. Spend With Pennies adds a can of beer, a halved lemon and bay leaves to the water, uses smoked sausage and serves it with baguette, lemon wedges and hot sauce. This follows Cooking Classy cut to 4 servings, with the milder smoked sausage from Spend With Pennies and its hot sauce on the side.
